signal_definition: Count of players marked Out or Doubtful on each side of the ball, plus a weighted practice trend (Did Not Participate = 0, Limited = 1, Full = 2) across report days
why_it_could_matter: Availability of a confirmed starter changes the expected lineup; the practice trend carries information the single game-status label does not
verification_now: Out/Doubtful counts by unit are verified for Week 10 (345 rows, re-checked field by field); practice trend needs more than one report version
data_needed: Multiple dated report versions per week (Tue/Wed/Thu) for the same game
leakage_risk: A forecast that uses Thursday's report to predict Thursday's line; use only the last report before the cutoff
test_statistic: Calibration slope of predicted vs realised margin, and mean absolute error vs a no-injury baseline

signal_definition: Difference between the confirmed starting lineup and the previous game's confirmed starting lineup for the same team and unit
why_it_could_matter: Measures a real lineup change instead of inferring one from a designation
verification_now: Official gamebooks publish starting lineups, substitutions, Did Not Play and Not Active lists; 19 starter-identity rows verified for WAS-NYG (Week 10)
data_needed: Gamebooks for consecutive weeks for both teams
leakage_risk: Using the game being predicted to define who started
time_available: Available after the previous game, before the next kickoff
test_statistic: Out-of-sample accuracy of a lineup-change indicator vs the designation-only baseline

signal_definition: Out-or-Doubtful players in a unit divided by the number of players the team lists at that unit
why_it_could_matter: Separates a single backup at a deep unit from several absences in the same meeting room
verification_now: Unit classification and exposure counts are verified; the denominator (players listed) is only the injury-report count, not roster size
data_needed: Official roster counts per position, or a licensed participation feed
leakage_risk: Reading the date of the roster snapshot as current
test_statistic: Unit-level win-probability effect with clustered uncertainty; report as unverified until measured

signal_definition: Number of confirmed starting offensive linemen who are Out, Doubtful or Not Active versus the previous game
why_it_could_matter: Line play is a shared dependency; a change there plausibly affects both the run game and the passing game
verification_now: Gamebook confirms which linemen started, including specific slots (LT/LG/C/RG/RT)
data_needed: Gamebooks across several weeks per team
leakage_risk: Treating a positional label as a lineup slot without checking the gamebook
time_available: Pregame once the inactive list is official
test_statistic: Coefficient stability and out-of-sample error against a line-neutral baseline

signal_definition: Confirmed starters at corner and safety who are Out, Doubtful or Not Active, plus the number of defensive backs the gamebook lists on the field at the start
why_it_could_matter: Backfield communication and coverage depend on who is actually on the field
verification_now: Gamebook lists the starting defensive alignment, including three safeties on some downs
data_needed: Gamebooks across several weeks per team
leakage_risk: Assuming the pregame depth order equals the game-day alignment
test_statistic: Out-of-sample forecast error by coverage group

signal_definition: Days of rest between games, derived from official kickoff dates, including Thursday games and the Munich international game
why_it_could_matter: Short rest is measurable from official dates and can interact with availability
verification_now: Official schedule provides exact dates and kickoff times for every game
data_needed: Several seasons of official schedules
leakage_risk: Using a game result to infer rest
test_statistic: Interaction term between rest and availability exposure, with clustered uncertainty

signal_definition: Neutral-site or international designation, roof type and surface, from official game information
why_it_could_matter: The Week 10 Munich game is an official international game with a stated venue; conditions are measurable
verification_now: International and venue designation is confirmed in the official schedule; weather is stated in the gamebook
data_needed: Official gamebook weather and venue fields across seasons
leakage_risk: Reading the forecast from the wrong date
test_statistic: Separate venue indicator, tested before any rule-conditioned model

signal_definition: Direction and magnitude of line movement from an authorized, timestamped price series
why_it_could_matter: Movement is information about how the market absorbed the same availability news
verification_now: No authorized odds feed exists in this repository; no movement value is stored or claimed
data_needed: A licensed historical closing- and opening-line archive with timestamps
leakage_risk: Leakage if closing prices are used as if they were available at the bet cutoff
time_available: Only at the timestamp the price was actually observed
test_statistic: Closing-line value distribution with bootstrap intervals

signal_definition: Pregame team scoring rate, opponent-adjusted defensive rate and pace, all built only from games before the cutoff
why_it_could_matter: A total is a sum, so it needs a joint scoring model rather than two independent point forecasts
verification_now: Official team and player statistics pages exist; no values are collected here
data_needed: Rights-cleared historical team and player statistics
leakage_risk: Building the feature from a season aggregate that includes the game being predicted
test_statistic: Out-of-sample error of the predicted total vs a league-mean baseline, with intervals

signal_definition: Explicit tag for the season's official playing rules that apply to the game
why_it_could_matter: Rule changes alter scoring and settlement; pooling seasons without a tag confounds the model
verification_now: The official NFL rulebook for the season is published
data_needed: The rulebook edition per season
leakage_risk: Silently pooling seasons with different rules
test_statistic: Nested test: pooled model vs rule-era-separated model

signal_definition: Whether the player was in the official starting lineup or listed as a substitution in the most recent game, plus the gamebook's recorded touches
why_it_could_matter: Props are about opportunity; a role change changes the opportunity distribution
verification_now: Gamebook starting lineups and substitutions give official role evidence for one Week 10 game
data_needed: Gamebook role data for many weeks
leakage_risk: Using the game being predicted to set the role
test_statistic: Predicted vs realised opportunity distribution, with calibration plots

signal_definition: Binary interaction between a player's own game status and a teammate's absence at the same unit
why_it_could_matter: A backup quarterback changes every receiving prop; a receiver absence changes target share
verification_now: The teammate absence side is verified; no player-level share values are collected
data_needed: Participation and target-share data with rights
leakage_risk: Definition drift between report and market settlement
test_statistic: Interaction improvement over a main-effect-only model, with multiplicity control

signal_definition: Whether a player appears in the Did Not Play list with a stated non-injury reason such as rest
why_it_could_matter: A rest designation is a different process from an injury and should not be pooled with one
verification_now: The Week 10 report contains explicit 'Not injury related - resting player' designations
data_needed: Several weeks of official reports
leakage_risk: Treating rest as injury severity
test_statistic: Separate coefficient for rest designations; test for pooling

signal_definition: Paired, settled outcomes for legs in the same game, with the joint event rate compared with the product of the marginals
why_it_could_matter: Parlay pricing is only defensible if dependence is measured, not assumed away
verification_now: No paired settleable data exists in the repository; nothing is calculated
data_needed: Rights-cleared settled prop outcomes with the exact market definitions
leakage_risk: Choosing legs from the same realized outcome
time_available: Must be set at the pregame cutoff
test_statistic: Joint rate minus product of marginals, with bootstrap interval and sample size

signal_definition: Number of legs in the same game that depend on the same team-level driver, such as the same quarterback
why_it_could_matter: Legs driven by one player are not independent even when their marginals look separate
verification_now: Leg definitions are known from the market description only when a licensed source is used
data_needed: Licensed market definitions and settled outcomes
leakage_risk: Counting legs as independent because the sportsbook prices them independently
test_statistic: Joint calibration of the full ticket vs the product of marginals

signal_definition: Brier-style score for the ticket's joint probability, compared with the independence benchmark
why_it_could_matter: Measures whether the joint model is calibrated rather than merely profitable by chance
verification_now: No score can be computed: there are no tested tickets
data_needed: Settled tickets with pregame probabilities recorded
leakage_risk: Scoring after the outcome is known with a rewritten probability
test_statistic: Brier score difference with bootstrap interval

signal_definition: Same-ticket legs from different games, with a test of whether the observed joint rate differs from the product of the marginals, allowing for shared week and season effects
why_it_could_matter: Cross-game legs share conditions such as weather and rest even when the games are separate
verification_now: Method defined; no observed joint rate exists
data_needed: Settled multi-game tickets
leakage_risk: Ignoring shared week-level conditions
test_statistic: Difference between joint and product-of-marginals, with clustered uncertainty

signal_definition: Explicit check of push, void and stat-correction rules for each leg before pricing a ticket
why_it_could_matter: A ticket's expected value changes with settlement rules; the rules are not derivable from a forecast
verification_now: No licensed rule text is attached to this project
data_needed: The provider's official rule text per market
leakage_risk: Modelling a push as a win or a loss
test_statistic: Reconciliation of modelled vs settled outcomes, leg by leg

signal_definition: Every input row carries a source URL and the exact observation time used in the forecast
why_it_could_matter: A forecast that cannot be replayed at its own timestamp cannot be verified
verification_now: The injury snapshot has per-row source links; the observation date is recorded as a day, and the page publishes no update time (Flag F13)
data_needed: An explicit capture timestamp per observation
leakage_risk: Rewriting a source after seeing the result
test_statistic: Percentage of rows with a source link and a timestamp, verified by the build

signal_definition: Every candidate is compared with a pre-declared baseline: league mean or the verified availability signal alone
why_it_could_matter: Without a baseline, any result looks like an edge
verification_now: No result is computed; the baseline rule is defined here
data_needed: Any rights-cleared evaluation set
leakage_risk: Raising the bar after seeing the result
test_statistic: Out-of-sample improvement over the declared baseline only
